claim: Traffic flow directly modulates signal timing through local feedback loops, with each intersection independently adjusting its green time based on immediate queue length measurements.
mechanism: Each intersection controller operates as an independent entity, continuously measuring queue length and vehicle count, then extending or reducing green time proportionally to these measurements without coordination with neighboring intersections.
evidence: Myxomycetes adapt tube diameter based on local flow without central coordination
Local traffic measurements are readily available at each intersection
assumptions: Queue length is the primary determinant of optimal green time
Local measurements provide sufficient information for optimal timing
Independent operation doesn't lead to system-wide oscillations
expected_failure_modes: Inability to adapt to network-wide congestion patterns
novelty_rationale: Applies direct local feedback from slime mold network adaptation to traffic signal control without inter-intersection coordination.
testability: Highly testable by implementing isolated intersection controllers with varying feedback gains and measuring performance metrics.
falsifier: If the system develops persistent oscillations in signal timing or shows reduced throughput compared to fixed timing, this hypothesis would be proven wrong as independent operation would fail to optimize network-level flow.
